title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: multicloud risk indicators
summary: The briefing accurately separates the roadmap plan from the documented preview and supports its opt-in default, licensing and usage-based billing. Minor improvements would extend the indicator path to its tab and identify checklist steps missing from the controls table.

claims.claim: This roadmap change belongs to Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview compliance portal: Insider Risk Management - Support for multicloud environments

claims.claim: The roadmap plans ready-to-use multicloud risk indicators for Azure, AWS, Box, Dropbox, Google Drive and GitHub.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management extends its detection into multicloud environments by offering ready-to-use risk indicators in Azure, AWS, and SaaS apps including Box, Dropbox, Google Drive, and GitHub.

claims.claim: The roadmap names data theft and data leaks policies as consumers of the indicators.
claims.quote: Organizations can use these new indicators in data theft and data leaks policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The Learn pages read do not name a built-in GitHub cloud indicator.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationales: risk, impact
claims.claim: The cloud indicators require administrator opt-in and are not in use if nobody enables them.
claims.quote: All global indicators are disabled by default; you must select one or more indicators to configure an Insider Risk Management policy.

claims.claim: Global indicator selection determines which indicators are available to policies.
claims.quote: Indicators enabled in global settings for Insider Risk Management define both the indicators available for configuration in policies and the types of events signals collected by Insider Risk Management.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; controls[0].note; controls[1].note
claims.claim: Relevant apps must first be connected in Microsoft Defender before their cloud indicators can be selected in Insider Risk Management.
claims.quote: To select from cloud indicators in Insider Risk Management settings and policies, you must first connect to the relevant cloud apps in Microsoft Defender, if you didn't already.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing; Scope; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Both cloud storage and cloud service indicators require pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Cloud storage indicators ... To use this indicator, enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization. ... Cloud service indicators ... To use this indicator, enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: Cloud storage and cloud service indicators are built-in indicators on the Built-in indicators tab.
claims.quote: Policy indicators are organized into two tabs: ... Built-in indicators ... Custom indicators ... Built-in indicators ... Cloud storage indicators ... Cloud service indicators

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management processes user activities corresponding to selected non-Microsoft 365 indicators in data theft and data leak policies to generate insights, alerts and cases.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management processes user activities corresponding to the non-Microsoft 365 indicators selected in data theft and data leak policies to generate insights, alerts, and cases.

claims.claim: Selected indicators make detected user activity from the documented cloud sources available for investigation.
claims.quote: After you configure indicators on the Insider Risk Management Settings page, the solution detects user activity for potentially risky activity associated with the selected indicators. This configuration makes all detected activity for users available for review

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Cloud storage indicators can be turned off per app, for example selecting content downloads for Box and Google Drive but not Dropbox.
claims.quote: After configuring the cloud storage indicators, you can turn off indicators for the apps you don't want to use in settings. For example, you can select a content download indicator for Box and Google Drive, but not Dropbox.

claims.claim: The roadmap says role-based access controls apply.

claims.quote: These instructions include the required permissions and authentication steps. Each cloud app has its own enablement process based on the APIs it supports.

claims.claim: Policy indicators determine a risk score for an in-scope user.
claims.quote: Policy indicators: Indicators included in Insider Risk Management policies determine a risk score for an in-scope user.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: Administrators must verify that the organisation has a supported Insider Risk Management subscription.
claims.quote: To access and use Insider Risk Management, administrators need to verify their organization has a supported subscription and assign the appropriate licenses to users.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: Appropriate Insider Risk Management licences must be assigned to users.
claims.quote: To access and use Insider Risk Management, administrators need to verify their organization has a supported subscription and assign the appropriate licenses to users.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed: user licensing together with consumption billing for cloud indicators.
claims.quote: The pay-as-you-go billing model builds on the per-user licensing model. The two are complementary, not mutually exclusive.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing is Azure based and requires associating the Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.
claims.quote: The billing mechanisms are Azure based, so you must associate your Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.

claims.claim: An Azure bill is generated at the end of the month.
claims.quote: An Azure bill is generated at the end of the month for the total number of pay-as-you-go charges across all Microsoft solutions.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: An Insider Risk Management processing unit represents the compute needed to process 10,000 relevant user activities.
claims.quote: For Insider Risk Management, a processing unit represents the compute required to process 10,000 such user activities. Billing is based on the number of processing units utilized.

claims.claim: The billing table gives the unit of measure as a Data Security processing unit measured daily.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management | Detect risky behavior for non-Microsoft 365 locations when using Cloud and generative AI policy indicators | Data Security processing unit as measured on a daily basis

claims.claim: Indicators for Box, Dropbox, Google Drive, AWS and Azure are billed on data security processing units.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management indicators that detect activity in cloud storage apps (Box, Dropbox, Google Drive), cloud services (AWS, Azure), and Microsoft Fabric (Power BI) are billed on data security processing units.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The change has variable, usage-based cost rather than a fixed or absent meter.
claims.quote: Billing is based on the number of processing units utilized.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Not yet published; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited Learn billing pages do not state a price per Insider Risk Management processing unit.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management processing unit price; read purview-billing-models and purview-billing-usage in full. They describe the meter and link to Azure pricing but give no price per IRM processing unit. This confirms only the page-scoped absence, not absence of Azure pricing.

claims.where: Scope: Clouds and platform; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited cloud-indicator pages do not specify which government clouds those indicators apply to.
claims.quote: Searched: cloud indicators GCC; Insider Risk Management cloud indicators GitHub GCC High DoD disable all. Read cloud sections of configure and policy-indicators and the GCC High plan table; none specifies cloud-indicator availability for GCC, GCC High or DoD.

claims.claim: The GCC High plan page's Insider Risk Management rows name no cloud storage or cloud service indicators.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management cloud indicators GCC High DoD; opened the cited plan-for-microsoft-purview-gcc-high-deployments page and read its IRM rows. They list Office, endpoint and other features, but no cloud storage or cloud service indicators.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Cloud indicators are configured in the Microsoft Purview portal at Insider Risk Management > Settings > Policy indicators.
claims.quote: In Insider Risk Management, go to Settings > Policy indicators ... Policy indicators are organized into two tabs: ... Built-in indicators
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct settings page but stops before its tab. Extend it to 'Insider Risk Management > Settings > Policy indicators > Built-in indicators', retaining the note that cloud storage and cloud service indicators are there, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-settings-policy-indicators.

claims.claim: No automation for selecting these built-in cloud indicators was found in Microsoft documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerShell insider risk management cloud policy indicators Set-InsiderRiskManagementPolicy indicators; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell InsiderRisk. Read policy-indicators and configure. Results document UI selection, not a cmdlet or API that sets these indicators.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The cited connector guide gives Microsoft Defender portal > Cloud Apps > Connected apps > Connect an app.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Defender portal. ... Go to Cloud Apps > Connected apps. ... Select Connect an app or Add a new connector.

claims.claim: The Defender get-started guide gives the alternative route Settings > Cloud Apps > Connected Apps > App Connectors > +Connect an app.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Defender Portal, select Settings. Then choose Cloud Apps. ... Under Connected Apps, select App Connectors. ... Select the +Connect an app to add an app and then select an app.

claims.claim: No documented automation for creating these Defender for Cloud Apps app connections was found.
claims.quote: Searched: defender cloud apps API create app connector connection automate. Opened the cited connector guide and defender-cloud-apps/api-introduction; its supported resources are activities, alerts, data enrichment, entities and files, not connector creation. Defender for Cloud is a different product.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go usage can be viewed in Microsoft Purview portal > Usage center > Pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: The Usage center in the Microsoft Purview portal helps you understand and manage your usage ... To access the Usage center > Pay-as-you-go ... pages

claims.claim: No documented automation equivalent to this Usage center surface was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Usage center API pay-as-you-go; Purview Usage center pay-as-you-go usage API spending limit Insider Risk Management. Opened purview-billing-usage and billing-models. No Usage center operation was documented; generic Azure cost exports are not an IRM feature pause or spending control.

claims.claim: Role group membership is edited at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Settings ... select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups ... Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "Insider Risk Management" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to that role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... The Member parameter specifies who you want to add ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go usage report is available in Insider Risk Management Reports.
claims.quote: The following reports are available by navigating to Insider Risk Management > Reports in the Microsoft Purview portal: ... Pay-as-you-go: Review pay-as-you-go usage reports

claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go report breaks down billed processing usage by data source category and activity indicator to support cost analysis.
claims.quote: The reports let you explore granular breakdowns of billed processing usage across different data source categories and activity indicators over time.

claims.claim: No single documented switch turns the multicloud capability on or off.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management cloud all disable; cloud indicators GitHub GCC High DoD disable all. Read policy-indicators, configure, connector guide and billing-usage. They document individual indicators, app connections and a nonpausable IRM usage entry, not a single multicloud switch.

claims.claim: Disabling relevant indicators or disconnecting the source app reduces incoming activity rather than pausing Insider Risk Management in the Usage center.
claims.quote: Once disabled, the connector instance stops consuming data from the connector.

claims.fix: The After rollout instruction to review the pay-as-you-go usage report has no matching controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet to align the checklist with the existing table; do not add a control row as part of this correction.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table

claims.fix: The At rollout instruction to add indicators to a policy and set thresholds has no matching policy-level control row. Remove that checklist bullet to align the checklist with the existing table; do not add a control row as part of this correction.
